scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths - success and failure - and a caller can tell which without parsing prose

evidence.asserts: The layer returns its declared envelope on BOTH paths, success and failure, and a caller can tell which without parsing prose. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source: http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts that error bodies carry all four envelope keys and that the HTTP status agrees with the body. A structural check - does the function import _shared/envelope.ts - would be the wrong prover here and R6 would refuse it, because importing the module is not the same as returning the envelope when the path fails.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - the envelope and the status agree with the body on all 40 relations probed. The gate also measures the harder half and reports it rather than hiding it: 27 of those relations CANNOT distinguish refusal from absence, which is PostgREST + RLS by construction rather than a defect patchable at the relation. What makes that acceptable is that every page reading them answers the question at its own layer, and the gate counts how: redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1. A prover returning a bare PASS over 40 relations while 27 were structurally ambiguous would assert more than it measured. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the gate, so a change to the functions or migrations under this claim still expires it; replay re-earns it in one command.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying data. Disagreement is measured on the wire, not inferred

evidence.asserts: The HTTP status and the body agree: no 200 carrying an error, no 4xx carrying a success. Proven by a registered gate that probes the LIVE gateway rather than by reading source - http_envelope issues real requests as anon, as a member and with no key, and asserts the status matches what the body actually says. This is the behavioural half of the envelope contract and cannot be settled structurally: a function can import the envelope helper and still answer 200 with an error inside, which is precisely the shape that makes a failed read look like an empty one to every caller downstream.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - status and body agree on all 40 relations probed, across anon, member and no-key callers. The gate reports what it cannot settle instead of smoothing it: 27 relations cannot distinguish refusal from absence, PostgREST + RLS by construction, each answered at the page layer rather than the relation (redirects-unauthenticated x19, anon-by-design x2, settles-auth-before-reads x1). That distinction matters more for THIS oracle than most, because a 200 carrying zero rows is exactly how a refusal disguises itself as an absence - the same class this platform hit when a failed read rendered as 'no contacts saved yet', and when a zero-row update returned no error and a reporter was told their report had been sent. depends_on names the subject artifacts as well as the prover, so a migration beneath the claim still expires it - as it did within this same session, when migration ...000068 landed after these rows were first banked and correctly staled the ones resting on migrations.

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the same call twice produces ONE effect; the second is refused or absorbed, and the count in the DB proves which

evidence.asserts: The same ordered read, issued twice over two SEPARATE connections, returns the same bytes: a repeat read is not quietly a different read. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - read_idempotency re-issues every repeatable read on the platform and compares a digest that is itself proven sensitive, so a match means agreement rather than a digest too coarse to notice a difference.
evidence.checked: Run live this session across all 22 pages: 93 repeatable reads, PASS - every repeatable read returned identical bytes across two separate connections. The sub-verdicts are carried here rather than flattened into the headline: 83 plain idempotent, 5 idempotent-uncontrolled (repeatable, but with no control proving the digest would have caught a change), 2 idempotent-modulo-clock, 2 CONTROL-FAILED and 1 UNKNOWN. Those last three are not passes and are recorded as such - a row claiming clean green while 3 reads never produced a verdict would be the vacuous match this gate exists to refuse.
evidence.value_checked: gate:read_idempotency | 93 repeatable reads across 22 pages, PASS | idempotent 83, uncontrolled 5, modulo-clock 2, control-failed 2, unknown 1 | digest proven sensitive | depends_on: analytics-report.html, tools/prove_read_idempotency.py, utils.js

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: a paginated or sorted read has a TOTAL order - re-running it does not reshuffle equal keys, so page 2 cannot repeat or skip a row from page 1

evidence.asserts: A paginated or sorted read at this layer has a TOTAL order: re-running it returns the same rows in the same sequence, so no row appears on two pages and none is skipped. Proven by a REGISTERED gate rather than a session - paginated-order-totality scans every paged-and-ordered query chain on the platform and fails if one ends without a unique tiebreaker, holding forward-only at 0. R2 turns this row INVALID rather than silently green if that gate is deleted or renamed.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: 176 paginated+ordered chains scanned platform-wide, 0 non-total, ratchet PASS at 0, and the gate's selftest passes BOTH directions - it catches a non-total order and accepts a tiebreakered one, which separates a working scanner from one that approves everything. The run also caught a regression introduced earlier in this same session (report-sender.html loadBounces ordering on triggered_at with no tiebreaker, 0 -> 1), fixed to .order('id') and back to 0. depends_on names the SUBJECT artifacts as well as the gate: anchoring to the gate alone was refused by R7, correctly - a page or migration that changes the query must expire the claim about it. Gate-backing buys a one-command recovery via replay, not immunity from staleness.
evidence.value_checked: gate:paginated-order-totality | 176 chains scanned, 0 non-total, forward-only PASS | selftest both directions | caught+fixed this session: report-sender.html:1357 order(triggered_at) | depends_on: analytics-report.html, tools/validate_paginated_order_totality.py, utils.js

scenarios.question: does each layer this page rests on honour its own contract - envelope, status/body agreement, idempotency, total ordering, declared units?
scenarios.oracle: the value carries its unit at the boundary (pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent) - the class that made a knob of 10 mean 1000%

evidence.asserts: A value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY - pesos vs credits vs percent vs whole-percent - so no consumer has to infer the scale. This is the class the oracle names as having made a knob of 10 mean 1000%. Proven by a registered gate: units_at_boundary requires every money, credit, percent and duration column to declare its unit by CHECK, comment, sibling unit column or name, and fails outright if any column mixes two scales.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS WITH DEBT, and the debt is recorded rather than rounded off. MIXED-SCALE = 0, the hard invariant that produces the 10-means-1000% failure. Two columns carry their unit only by convention and are reported, not failed: conversation_analytics.answer_quality_rating (percent) and service_credit_ledger.amount (money), each with no CHECK, no comment, no sibling unit column and a name that does not say; five more are undecl-latent. Those seven are real debt against this oracle and are named so they can be closed rather than rediscovered. The gate was matched to the oracle deliberately: the oracle says the value carries its unit AT THE BOUNDARY and names the mixed-scale failure, which is this gate's subject - the neighbouring prove_units_visible answers a different question (what a reader sees) and would have been the wrong prover.

findings.detail: MEASURED AND FAILING - the edge layer's error envelope is not machine-readable, and it is not shaped like the db layer's. Two concrete defects, both measured against the local edge runtime this session: (1) an edge function's error body is {"error": "<prose>"} with NO machine-readable `code` field, so a caller can only pattern-match English to decide what happened - while the SAME platform's db layer returns {code, details, hint, message} for every failure class (400 bad column, 404 unknown table, 401 no grant), which a client CAN branch on. One product, two incompatible error contracts. (2) a routing 404 (unknown function name) is returned as **text/plain**, so `res.json()` THROWS rather than yielding an error object - the caller's catch block sees a SyntaxError about unexpected token, not a 404, and any code that checks `data.error` never runs. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this is the layer behind the AI gateway, the orchestrators, OCR/voice capture and report generation. A client that treats db and edge errors alike - which the identical-looking `.error` property invites - will mishandle one of them, and the failure mode is the one this bank keeps finding: an exception swallowed into an empty render, indistinguishable from a server that honestly answered nothing. LEFT OWED RATHER THAN GREEN, DELIBERATELY: the oracle asks that status and body AGREE and that the envelope be uniform, and it does not. Banking it green would be a false green; recording it owed with the diagnosis is the honest state. TO FINISH: return JSON for routing 404s (Content-Type application/json), and add a stable `code` alongside `error` in every edge error body, then re-walk. That is an edge-function change and belongs in a batched wave, not mid-walk.

findings.title: banked green for a non-HTTP layer on evidence taken only at the PostgREST gateway - the edge envelope is demonstrably a different shape
findings.detail: I banked envelope_shape and status_body_agreement for EVERY layer subject on one measurement: real GETs against http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1. That measurement is sound for the client/gateway/db layers and says NOTHING about this row's layer. The proof that it is a different question, taken minutes later once the edge runtime was restarted: POST {} to /functions/v1/ai-gateway answers 400 with the body {"error":"Missing agent"} - ONE key. The PostgREST envelope this row was banked on is {code, message, details, hint} - FOUR keys, and the row's own evidence asserts all four are present. So the edge layer does not satisfy the property this row was marked green for, and if it had been probed the verdict might well have been a finding. HOW IT HAPPENED: the banker iterated every CA layer row on the page and applied the same gateway result to all of them, using R7/page_layer_deps to get the DEPENDENCIES right while never checking that the MEASUREMENT matched the layer. Correct anchoring on the wrong evidence still yields a false green - an oracle that does not match its claim. AND THE EDGE RUNTIME WAS DOWN THE WHOLE TIME: supabase_edge_runtime_workhive had been 'Exited (255) 4 days ago', so at the moment of banking every edge function on the platform was answering 503. A layer claim banked while that layer is not running cannot be anything but false, and nothing in the banker noticed - the reading came from a different service that WAS up. `docker start` brought it back and it now serves 58 functions. TO RE-EARN: probe the layer this row actually names. For edge/ai/external-send that is /functions/v1/<fn> with apikey + a member JWT (tools/backend_edge_probe.py has the helpers; note its anon_key() returns '' on this stack because it only accepts legacy eyJ JWTs - prove_http_envelope.resolve_key() carries the working fallback). For cron/realtime/print/cdn the envelope question needs its own instrument and the row should stay owed until one exists, rather than inheriting a reading from whatever service happened to answer.

THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself.

scenarios.oracle: what one side of the seam WRITES is what the other side READS - compared value-to-value against psql, never screen-to-screen

evidence.asserts: What one side of the seam WRITES is what the other side READS: a value is not silently rewritten on the way in by something nobody named. Proven by a registered gate rather than a session - values_survive_write extracts every trigger that assigns to NEW, classifies the rewrite by its STRUCTURE, and fails on any that belongs to no named class. It also measures the one class that can lose a person's work: every left(NEW.col, N) cap is read against the stored data, because a possible truncation and an actual one are different facts.
evidence.checked: Run live this session: PASS - every rewrite on the way in belongs to a named class, and none of the 106 capped columns has ever truncated a stored value (widest: engineering_calcs.sow_text at 984 of 4000). It earned that by first FAILING on a trigger I had added earlier in this same session: tg_community_posts_moderation_fields, which restores flagged/pinned for a caller who is not a supervisor of that hive (migrations ...000063/64, after a reported author was found clearing their own flag). The gate was right to stop it - it assigns NEW.x := OLD.x, a shape none of its four classes covered. The fix was to teach the CLASSIFIER a new structural class, field-authorization-guard, not to rename my trigger guard_* to slip past a prefix check: the function's own docstring says widening the name allowlist until the gate goes green is bending the gate, and structure is what a rewrite DOES. The new class is detected on shape - every assignment restoring the column to its own prior value - so no outside value replaces the caller's and their other edits still land.

findings.detail: FAILS: with 3 reads answered 500, this page renders **372 characters and says nothing at all about the failure** - no sentence, no dash sentinel, no retry. This page's render target is PAPER - a printed report - so a silent empty render is the one failure mode that can be distributed before anyone notices. A SILENT SURFACE IS AN EMPTY ANSWER. Someone opening it during a backend fault cannot tell it from a page with nothing in it. NINE PAGES IN THIS SWEEP ANSWER THE SAME INJECTION WITH A SENTENCE (hive, inventory, dayplanner, pm-scheduler, index, skillmatrix, achievements, voice-journal, assistant), so the instrument discriminates and this is the page. MEASURED BY ANSWERING EVERY READ WITH A 500 AT window.fetch AND READING WHAT THE PAGE SAYS NEXT. Each `/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/` request resolves to a synthetic `{"code":"500"}` with Content-Type application/json; `/auth/v1/` is untouched so the session survives, which is what makes this a SERVER fault rather than a dead network. Interceptions are counted and a verdict over zero failed reads is refused as vacuous. Every claim below quotes the page's own visible sentence, collected from leaf-ish elements under a composed-visibility test (getClientRects + checkVisibility + an ancestor walk for display/visibility/opacity) so hidden template copy cannot be mistaken for something a reader sees. TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS SWEEP WERE THROWN AWAY, WHICH IS WHY THE NUMBERS HERE ARE TRUSTED. The first used Playwright's `route()` and intercepted **0** requests on all 8 pages while they rendered live data - a registered service worker sits between page and transport in a warm context, so route() never saw the calls. The second omitted the identity guard and returned byte-identical output for seven different pages (14,677 chars of marketing copy) because the session had expired and every page had redirected to `index.html?signin=1`. This version guards INSIDE the evaluate: expected uid, `location.pathname` ends in the page's own file, and body chars outside the 13,000-16,000 landing band - refusing rather than reporting. Only 2 offer a retry CONTROL (achievements, community); public-feed's was measured firing a real re-request and rendering 15 posts.

findings.detail: FINDING RETRACTED - MEASURED ON AN UNARRIVED SURFACE. I recorded analytics-report as rendering '372 characters and saying nothing about the failure', weighted by the observation that this page's render target is PAPER and a silent empty report can be distributed before anyone notices. **The healthy control renders the same 369 characters.** The page presents an identical minimal surface whether its reads succeed or are all answered 500, which means what was measured is the page BEFORE it has been asked for anything - a shell, exactly like project-report without a `?project_id=`. A 'silent under failure' verdict over a shell describes the shell. WHAT A VALID MEASUREMENT NEEDS: establish how this page is ARRIVED at - which query parameter or generate action populates it (project-report needed `?project_id=`, asset-hub needed `?tag=`) - load it populated, confirm the surface grew beyond the shell band, and only then inject. The arrival is typically one URL parameter, so this is a one-call unit rather than a blocker. Its own CD invariants ('the print render contains every section the screen shows', 'a page break never separates a finding from its evidence') are unreachable until then too, so the arrival is the gating unit for this whole page. WHY BOTH READINGS ARE UNSOUND, AND HOW IT WAS CAUGHT: the failed run and the HEALTHY control produced BYTE-COMPARABLE output. If injecting a 500 into every read changes nothing a reader can see, the injection did not reach what the page renders - so no verdict about its failure behaviour is available from that run, in either direction. Running the healthy control alongside is what exposed it; the original sweep ran only the failure case and read its output as a property of the page. THIS IS THE SECOND TIME TODAY THE SAME METHODOLOGICAL GAP FIRED. analytics was likewise recorded as 'silent under failure' when the injection pattern (`/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/`) never matched its `/functions/v1/` orchestrator path - and the page in fact says 'Analytics unavailable' with dashed heroes. A pass/fail over an untouched data path is the vacuous-injection shape the delayed-read probe already guards against by counting interceptions and refusing a verdict over zero; that guard belongs in the failure probe too, plus a healthy control on every page, which is now the standing method.

findings.detail: FAILS: 8 call(s) failed and the page said NOTHING about it (369 chars healthy -> 369 chars failed). THE ORACLE IS A DIFFERENCE, NOT A STRING, inherited from the marketplace spec this extends: the page is read HEALTHY first, and a pass requires the failure wording to APPEAR - if the healthy render already said it, the words were always there and prove nothing, so the page is UNGRADED. A pass therefore means the page answered a broken read with something failure-shaped that it does not say when healthy. FOUR WAYS TO FAIL IT: rendering EMPTINESS ('no items', 'nothing here') for a failure - the two are indistinguishable to a person and one of them is a lie, and this platform shipped exactly that when public-feed's Retry answered 'No public posts yet' over 15 existing posts; leaving a SKELETON shimmering at someone whose data will never arrive; saying nothing at all; or being ungraded because the injection never fired. The vocabulary is IMPORTED from session_signals.mjs, harvested from this product's own sentences - the spec's own note is that an oracle recognising only its author's phrasing measures vocabulary, not behaviour. ★ THREE OF THE SEVEN MODES CARRY THEIR OWN PASS CONDITION, because 'did a failure message appear?' is the right question for only four of them, and using one assertion for all seven is how a family looks green while asserting the wrong thing on three of its members. fail_slow is a SUCCESSFUL read that is merely late: demanding a failure message there would be demanding a LIE. It must show the page is WORKING - a skeleton, spinner or busy state - and it is sampled MID-FLIGHT, at 2.5s of a 6s delay, because by the time the data lands the answer has been erased; a final-state read would score a page that showed a blank screen for six seconds identically to one that showed a skeleton. fail_null_field is not an error at all - the rows arrive and their non-id fields are null - so the only question is whether the page prints `null`, `undefined` or `NaN` at a person. The nulls are applied to the REAL response rather than to a synthesised one, so the test exercises the page's own schema instead of this prover's idea of it, and the match is word-bounded so 'Nullarbor' or a part code containing 'nan' cannot trip it. fail_partial is a 200 whose JSON does not parse - what a connection dropped mid-transfer actually looks like - and must read as a failure rather than as 'no rows'. WHAT THE NULL MODE ACTUALLY FOUND, verified page by page rather than inferred from a sweep line: three pages print a raw null at a person, and all three share ONE shape - a `|| fallback` present on one interpolation and missing on its NEIGHBOUR in the same template literal. inventory:1542 `Available: ${item.qty_on_hand} ${item.unit || 'pcs'}` renders OUT OF STOCK null pcs eight times: the UNIT fell back, the QUANTITY did not - the page guards the decoration and leaves the number a technician acts on unguarded. alert-hub:611 `shift ${brief.shift_date} · model ${brief.model_version || 'amc-v1'}` prints `shift null` while rendering `(no headline)` two lines later, so the idiom was in hand at the time. skillmatrix:854 `Primary: ${_profile.primary_skill} · ${WORKER_NAME}` prints `Primary: null · Leandro Marquez` - a raw null in a person's DISCIPLINE, beside their name, on the surface whose job is stating their qualifications. THE CONSEQUENCES DIFFER AND ARE NOT FLATTENED: a wrong quantity, a wrong claim about a person, a wrong shift on a supervisor's brief. One habit, three one-token corrections - not a design decision. HOW THE FAILURE IS INDUCED, and why the method is the hard part: every Supabase REST/RPC call is failed at window.fetch, patched via addInitScript so it is in place BEFORE any page script runs. That timing is the whole trick. tests/failure-injection.spec.ts records that replacing window.fetch AFTER load never fires, because supabase-js captures fetch when the CLIENT IS CONSTRUCTED - so it used page.route instead; this project separately learned that page.route is bypassed by a warm SERVICE WORKER serving from cache. Both are true, and the reconciliation is WHEN THE PATCH LANDS: an init script is not a late override, and it sits above the service worker rather than below it. THE INJECTION COUNTS ITS OWN HITS and a page where the counter reads zero is UNGRADED, never judged - because a failure-injection oracle that does not inject produces the most convincing false findings available: 'the page said nothing about the error' is exactly what a page with NO error would say. WHAT THIS ORACLE FOUND ON ITS FIRST RUN, and it was a hole in a fix made earlier the same day: the central transport notice hung off `.then(res => ...)`, so a REJECTED or ABORTED fetch - which never produces a res - skipped it entirely. Status-bearing failures (500/401) were covered; transport failures were not. Measured on logbook: 13 rejected reads, ZERO page errors, ZERO console errors, and not one word on screen - the page caught the rejection and dropped it, which is the '118 annotated empty-catch blocks across 11 pages' habit utils.js already documents. FIXED at the transport in a `.catch` that NOTICES AND RE-THROWS, because that wrapper's own comment forbids a catch that swallows the error callers must surface; `throw err` leaves every caller's {data, error} untouched. Timeout and offline get DIFFERENT sentences, since 'check your connection' is useless advice for one and the only useful advice for the other; the connection notice IS cleared by the next successful read (the network is demonstrably back) while the permission notice deliberately is not. THREE INSTRUMENT CORRECTIONS BEHIND THIS ROW, each of which had produced a confident false FAIL. (1) The first version waited 9s for a timeout the platform bounds at 15s (whQueryTimeout, utils.js:1785) - measuring its own impatience and reporting 'the page said NOTHING', a true statement about an instant nobody experiences. (2) Widening the wait revealed that whQueryTimeout is adopted by only SIX surfaces (community, public-feed and the four marketplace pages), so on these 20 pages the only bound is the transport abort at WH_DB_TIMEOUT_MS || 45000; rather than idle 45s per page the prover sets that documented knob to 4s, which utils.js:703 explicitly invites ('tune via window.WH_DB_TIMEOUT_MS'). (3) The hang stub IGNORED THE ABORT SIGNAL, so the platform's own timeout became a no-op and the page sat silent forever - the stub was suppressing the exact mechanism under test. A fake fetch must emulate CANCELLATION, not just latency. SCOPE: V1 only - the page as it loads, signed in as supervisor - across all seven CC modes. The V2 view is a separate row and is NOT claimed here. community and public-feed are excluded because tests/failure-injection.spec.ts already walks them. NON-WRITING: only reads are failed; nothing is typed or submitted.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_source_chip.mjs, live: 41 views graded across the roster - 18 make a TRUE provenance claim, 23 make NO claim, 0 name a feed they never read. THE ORACLE MATTERS MORE THAN MOST UI TEXT: a source chip is a promise that a number came from named feeds, and a reader uses it to decide whether to trust the figure. A chip naming a feed the page never queried is worse than no chip, because it manufactures confidence. SO THE CLAIM IS CHECKED AGAINST THE NETWORK, not the source: every PostgREST /rest/v1/<relation> the view actually requests is captured at runtime, and each schema-shaped token the chip names must correspond to one. It is deliberately ONE-DIRECTIONAL - a chip that SUMMARISES is fine, a chip that INVENTS is not. ★TWO MANUFACTURED FINDINGS WERE CAUGHT AND REMOVED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS BANKED. The first version of the token test counted the bare word `logbook`, so asset-hub and analytics were both reported as naming an unread feed - on the strength of ordinary prose: 'Based on your asset records, risk scores, logbook, failure analysis'. That is a sentence describing FEATURES to a person, not an assertion about a table, and analytics is right on its own terms - it reads analytics_snapshots, a snapshot DERIVED from logbook data, which is precisely what 'saved snapshot ... based on your logbook' says. A keyword match over human prose is how a page's own helper text becomes a defect. The test now counts a token only when it is unmistakably schema-shaped (a v_ prefix, a _truth suffix, or a known table prefix + underscore); bare English words never qualify. ★AND THE VIEW IS READ INSIDE ITSELF. V1 is graded at page scope and V2 inside the OPENED view via the shared tools/dialog_targets.mjs registry, because crediting a V2 row with a V1 reading is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error this bank has already paid for once. NOT BANKED GREEN: this view displays NO source chip at all (0 on screen while the surface requested 5 relation(s)). A surface that makes no provenance claim has not made a TRUE one, and the oracle asks whether the claim is true - so silence cannot satisfy it. Scoring it green would credit the absence of a promise as a kept promise. THIS IS ALSO NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT. Most of the 23 are V2 dialogs - a composer, a confirm sheet, a detail panel - which display a form rather than a derived figure, and a provenance chip on a surface that states no number would be noise. WHAT SETTLES IT is the per-view question the bank actually asks: does THIS view show a figure a reader would want provenance for? If yes, the chip is missing and this is a real finding; if no, the row is declared-na under R10 with 'this view states no derived figure' as the reason and the CM comprehension oracles as its replacement. Left owed rather than guessed, because that question is per-view and answering it from a count would be inventing the verdict.

findings.detail: FAILS: with 3 reads answered 500, **no retry control is present** - zero visible elements whose label mentions retry or try-again. It says nothing at all about the failure (372 visible characters). SO THE ONLY RECOURSE IS A FULL RELOAD, which on a phone in a plant costs the whole page again on the connection that just failed. THE PATTERN EXISTS ON THIS PLATFORM, so this is adoption: achievements renders a Retry button beside its toast, and public-feed's Retry was measured firing a real re-request and then rendering 15 post cards. Only 2 of 22 pages have one. WHAT WOULD PASS IT: a control that RE-ISSUES the failed read - the probe counts requests fired after the click, so a button that merely re-renders the previous failure fails too. That is the exact defect commit 3ddef99d fixed on public-feed. MEASURED BY ANSWERING EVERY READ WITH A 500 AT window.fetch AND READING WHAT THE PAGE SAYS NEXT. Each `/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/` request resolves to a synthetic `{"code":"500"}` with Content-Type application/json; `/auth/v1/` is untouched so the session survives, which is what makes this a SERVER fault rather than a dead network. Interceptions are counted and a verdict over zero failed reads is refused as vacuous. Every claim below quotes the page's own visible sentence, collected from leaf-ish elements under a composed-visibility test (getClientRects + checkVisibility + an ancestor walk for display/visibility/opacity) so hidden template copy cannot be mistaken for something a reader sees. TWO EARLIER VERSIONS OF THIS SWEEP WERE THROWN AWAY, WHICH IS WHY THE NUMBERS HERE ARE TRUSTED. The first used Playwright's `route()` and intercepted **0** requests on all 8 pages while they rendered live data - a registered service worker sits between page and transport in a warm context, so route() never saw the calls. The second omitted the identity guard and returned byte-identical output for seven different pages (14,677 chars of marketing copy) because the session had expired and every page had redirected to `index.html?signin=1`. This version guards INSIDE the evaluate: expected uid, `location.pathname` ends in the page's own file, and body chars outside the 13,000-16,000 landing band - refusing rather than reporting. PLATFORM RESULT, all 22 pages: **9 state the failure in domain language** (hive, inventory, dayplanner, pm-scheduler, index, skillmatrix, achievements, voice-journal, assistant) and **11 say nothing or assert a falsehood**. Only 2 offer a retry CONTROL (achievements, community); public-feed's was measured firing a real re-request and rendering 15 posts.

findings.title: MEASURED with live-state-runner.js::availability({settle:1500}) driven across the whole product roster by tools/prove_availability_pages.mjs - the SAME lens tools/walk_owed_scenarios.mjs uses for the marketplace surfaces, so the two banks cannot disagree about what these words mean.
findings.detail:
MEASURED with live-state-runner.js::availability({settle:1500}) driven across the whole product roster by tools/prove_availability_pages.mjs - the SAME lens tools/walk_owed_scenarios.mjs uses for the marketplace surfaces, so the two banks cannot disagree about what these words mean. ★THE INDUCTION IS PROVEN TO HAVE LANDED, which is the difference between a verdict and a guess: the lens reports inductionLanded, the number of reads that actually went out under the injected condition, and refuses to score a page that never re-queried. Its own comment records why - it once read retry_path:false / fallback:silentlyStale on a surface that handles both correctly, because closure-scoped loaders meant the page never moved, and it scored the UNCHANGED page. Every verdict banked here carries inductionLanded > 0 and inconclusive:false. ★AND THE LENS IS PROVEN ABLE TO PASS, so a FAIL is not a blanket instrument failure: across the roster it returned retry_path 3 PASS / 19 FAIL, rate_limit_legible 1/21, fallback_engaged 7/15, slow_honest 10/12. public-feed passes all four - consistent with its own history, since it is the page fixed so a failed read renders an error rather than 'No public posts yet'. RETRY PATH - FAILS, and the half that is certain is the half that matters. Under an injected 500 this page offers ZERO retry affordances: no 'try again', no 'reload', no 'refresh' control. That is confirmed TWO independent ways - the lens counted affordances:0, and a separate direct probe that 500'd every /rest/v1/ request and scanned the whole document for a retry control also found none. A person whose data failed to load has nothing to press. ★ONE HALF OF THIS VERDICT IS INSTRUMENT-DEPENDENT AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH RATHER THAN BANKED AS FACT: the lens also reported saysFailure:False. My direct probe, which failed EVERY read rather than the subset the lens induces, and which scanned the whole page rather than <main>, found that this page DOES say something failed under a total outage. So the page's failure MESSAGING may be better than the lens's number suggests - a partial induction can leave a surface half-populated and quiet. The missing retry CONTROL is not in doubt; the missing failure SENTENCE is, on this page. WHY IT IS NOT BANKED GREEN ANYWAY: the oracle asks for a retry PATH, and a failure a person cannot act on is the shape this family exists to catch - 'a failure that offers a retry which does not re-attempt is worse than one that offers none', and offering none at all is the floor of that same scale.

★RETRACTED CONTEXT ON THIS ROW'S RECORDED TALLY: it lists rate_limit_legible as 1P/21F. That figure is true of THIS LENS and misleading about the platform, and is retracted as evidence of any gap. 42 rate_limit_legible rows are banked green on a 2026-08-09 induction against the REAL limit - 400 logbook inserts inside BEGIN...ROLLBACK as an authenticated member, refused with 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' plus HINT logbook_daily_user, and a second hive-tier quota at SQLSTATE 54000 that states its remedy. THE PLATFORM'S RATE LIMITING IS LEGIBLE. This lens asked a different question - whether a page's TEXT names a limit under a FAKE 429 injected at the fetch layer, a client-rendering question about a condition the server never produced. PRECEDENCE (roadmap 6l/6m): a prover that induced the REAL condition outranks a lens that simulated one; the disagreement is scope, never regression. THE VERDICT ON THIS ROW'S OWN KEY IS UNAFFECTED - it rests on its own induction, which landed (inductionLanded > 0).

observed.excluded: offline_refusal - a dedicated prover outranks this lens (see roadmap 6l)

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_retry_path.mjs (new) - EVERY /rest/v1/ read failed with a 500, then the network released and the retry pressed.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_retry_path.mjs (new) - EVERY /rest/v1/ read failed with a 500, then the network released and the retry pressed. ★THE INDUCTION IS TOTAL, NOT PARTIAL, AND THAT CHANGED THE ANSWER. The availability lens fails a SUBSET of reads and reported 'affordances: 0' for pages that demonstrably DO render a Retry on other paths. Failing every request is what actually reaches a page's error branch. ★AND BOTH CLAUSES ARE MEASURED, because the second is the one that ships broken: a retry must RE-ATTEMPT and the failure must CLEAR. hive proved why - its first fix sent 3 fresh reads and left the page byte-for-byte unchanged, because it re-rendered from a cache still holding the failed state. A retry that re-attempts and does not recover is worse than none: it invites pressing again. ★THE ROSTER, so no page's verdict rests on its own reading alone: PASS 6 (hive, logbook, inventory, skillmatrix, public-feed, resume) | NO-RETRY 9 | NO-RECOVER 3 | NO-ATTEMPT 1 | SILENT 3. ★THE COMPONENT ALREADY EXISTS - THIS IS ADOPTION, NOT DESIGN. whListError(el, message, onRetry) in utils.js renders the inline error WITH a working Retry, and 16 pages already import it. findings.title: The DB's legible rate-limit message is likely MASKED by a generic client string on the write path
findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. But the client does not necessarily show it. logbook.html:1885 renders save failures as a fixed string - 'Could not save. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. So the platform can produce a genuinely good limit message and still tell the reader to retry immediately. This is the mirror image of a defect fixed earlier in this same session, where pages echoed the RAW upstream message to the reader: the lesson is not 'always show the server string' nor 'never show it', but that a write path needs to distinguish a LIMIT (legible, actionable, has a reset time) from a FAULT (retry may work) - and the HINT key exists precisely so it can. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE on this row because the oracle asks whether the rate limit is legible, and at the layer that produces it, it is - verifiably, with a machine-readable key. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

evidence.asserts: when a limit is hit the refusal is legible - it names the limit, the scope, and when it clears, and carries a machine-readable key so a client can tell WHICH limit fired
evidence.checked: FIRED FOR REAL, NOT READ FROM THE SOURCE - and then the source was read to confirm the second tier. Inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member (role SET, not just claims), a burst of 400 logbook inserts was attempted. The trigger refused with: **'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.'** carrying HINT 'logbook_daily_user'. Verified clean afterwards: 0 probe rows survived the rollback. WHY THIS COUNTS AS LEGIBLE, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE: it names the LIMIT (100), names WHAT was hit (today's free limit, i.e. a per-user daily cap rather than a system fault), tells the reader WHEN IT CLEARS ('Resets at midnight') so they know whether to wait or escalate, and ships a machine-readable HINT key ('logbook_daily_user') so a client can branch on WHICH limit fired instead of pattern-matching English. That combination - human sentence plus stable key - is what separates a legible limit from 'permission denied'. THERE IS A SECOND TIER AND IT IS ALSO LEGIBLE: check_hive_quota_logbook raises 'logbook cumulative quota exceeded for hive % (% >= %)' with ERRCODE 54000 and a HINT that old records can be archived - so the per-user daily cap and the per-hive cumulative quota are distinguishable by SQLSTATE and by message, and the hive-level one tells the reader the remedy (archive) rather than just the fact. ANCHORED ON supabase/migrations PER A13 - the message lives in the trigger body.

FALLBACK ENGAGED - FAILS. under failure the page neither engaged a visible fallback nor said it was showing saved data. PRECEDENCE (roadmap 6l/6m): a prover that induced the REAL condition outranks a lens that simulated one; the disagreement is scope, never regression. THE VERDICT ON THIS ROW'S OWN KEY IS UNAFFECTED - it rests on its own induction, which landed (inductionLanded > 0).

findings.title: The DB's legible rate-limit message is likely MASKED by a generic client string on the write path
findings.detail: The refusal this row banks on is excellent AT ITS SOURCE: 'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.' with HINT logbook_daily_user. But the client does not necessarily show it. logbook.html:1885 renders save failures as a fixed string - 'Could not save. Check your connection and try again.' - which is not only generic but WRONG for this case: the connection is fine, the person hit a daily cap, and 'try again' is the one instruction guaranteed to fail until midnight. So the platform can produce a genuinely good limit message and still tell the reader to retry immediately. This is the mirror image of a defect fixed earlier in this same session, where pages echoed the RAW upstream message to the reader: the lesson is not 'always show the server string' nor 'never show it', but that a write path needs to distinguish a LIMIT (legible, actionable, has a reset time) from a FAULT (retry may work) - and the HINT key exists precisely so it can. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE on this row because the oracle asks whether the rate limit is legible, and at the layer that produces it, it is - verifiably, with a machine-readable key. TO FINISH: on the write error path, branch on the hint/SQLSTATE (logbook_daily_user, 54000) and surface the server's own sentence plus its reset time instead of the connection string. Then re-walk this oracle at the client layer.

evidence.asserts: when a limit is hit the refusal is legible - it names the limit, the scope, and when it clears, and carries a machine-readable key so a client can tell WHICH limit fired
evidence.checked: FIRED FOR REAL, NOT READ FROM THE SOURCE - and then the source was read to confirm the second tier. Inside BEGIN ... ROLLBACK as an authenticated member (role SET, not just claims), a burst of 400 logbook inserts was attempted. The trigger refused with: **'You have logged today's free limit (100). Resets at midnight.'** carrying HINT 'logbook_daily_user'. Verified clean afterwards: 0 probe rows survived the rollback. WHY THIS COUNTS AS LEGIBLE, CLAUSE BY CLAUSE: it names the LIMIT (100), names WHAT was hit (today's free limit, i.e. a per-user daily cap rather than a system fault), tells the reader WHEN IT CLEARS ('Resets at midnight') so they know whether to wait or escalate, and ships a machine-readable HINT key ('logbook_daily_user') so a client can branch on WHICH limit fired instead of pattern-matching English. That combination - human sentence plus stable key - is what separates a legible limit from 'permission denied'. THERE IS A SECOND TIER AND IT IS ALSO LEGIBLE: check_hive_quota_logbook raises 'logbook cumulative quota exceeded for hive % (% >= %)' with ERRCODE 54000 and a HINT that old records can be archived - so the per-user daily cap and the per-hive cumulative quota are distinguishable by SQLSTATE and by message, and the hive-level one tells the reader the remedy (archive) rather than just the fact. ANCHORED ON supabase/migrations PER A13 - the message lives in the trigger body.

findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. Writing as Hector (JWT sub 8fb252f7-...) while supplying auth_uid = Romeo's id AND worker_name = 'Romeo Beltran': the stored auth_uid was corrected to Hector's by trg_bind_submitter_logbook, and the stored worker_name remained 'Romeo Beltran'. So the authoritative identity is safe and the human-readable one is not. WHY THAT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY, RATHER THAN AS A PURIST POINT: reads across this platform filter and group by worker_name, not by auth_uid - `.eq('worker_name', WORKER_NAME)` is the dominant pattern in logbook, inventory, dayplanner, skillmatrix and the resume evidence path. So a row whose worker_name disagrees with its auth_uid is attributed to the WRONG PERSON in every list that reads it, while looking perfectly consistent to any check that only inspects auth_uid. logbook is the platform's evidence base: it feeds MTBF, PM compliance and a person's resume evidence, so misattribution is not cosmetic. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. The first is the smaller change and keeps the existing read patterns working.

evidence.asserts: every piece of edge-pinned chrome declares a safe-area inset for ITS OWN edge - read from the AUTHORED CSS over CDP (inline style, attribute style, and every matched rule), not from getComputedStyle, which flattens an unapplied env() to 0px and would report a missing declaration as satisfied
evidence.checked: 2026-08-20 gate:cj_safe_area - clean full run: 22 pages, every edge-pinned element resolved, decoration and modal overlays excluded and COUNTED as skips rather than silently dropped
evidence.value_checked:
the direction is part of the claim: top-pinned chrome needs inset-top, bottom-pinned needs inset-bottom, so a direction-blind match cannot pass this. Falsifiable by a planted bottom-pinned element with no inset (caught as uncovered) beside one carrying env(safe-area-inset-bottom) (correctly clean) - and the satisfier proves the CDP path really does see an inline env(), which it must, since coverage reads inlineStyle.cssText first

findings.title: NOT BANKED - states() blocks the page MAIN THREAD here. Proven: a setTimeout(20000) inside the page NEVER FIRED
findings.detail: THREE attempts, each aborted by the harness at 1800s: once inside a 6-page batch, once as an isolated evaluate on a freshly navigated tab, and once wrapped in an explicit Promise.race against a 20-SECOND setTimeout. That third attempt is the decisive one and it overturns my earlier hypothesis. I had recorded this as "a promise that never settles", the known invisible-hang class on this platform. It is NOT. A pending promise would have lost the race to a 20s timer; that timer NEVER FIRED, and a setTimeout cannot fire while the main thread is busy. So this is a SYNCHRONOUS main-thread block, not an unresolved await - which is a different defect with a different fix, and no amount of timeout wrapping can bound it from inside the page. WHAT THE PROBE DOES THAT COULD CAUSE IT: states() cannot observe loading/skeleton on a settled page so it INDUCES them, and part of that induction is document.dispatchEvent(new Event("DOMContentLoaded")) to re-fire the page loaders. Re-running init on a page whose init is not idempotent is the obvious candidate for an unbounded synchronous loop, and both pages that block are REPORT surfaces that build their content through an orchestrator on init. STATED AS THE LEADING CANDIDATE, NOT AS PROVEN - I have not isolated it, because each attempt costs 1800s of wall clock and I have now spent three. NOTE WHAT IS NOT WRONG: the page itself is healthy. It navigates, renders, and its contrast_wcag, contrast_apca, tap_target_44, w390/w641/w1280_overflow, safe_area and focus_visible rows ALL walked clean today. Only this probe blocks on it. HOW TO RESOLVE WITHOUT BURNING ANOTHER HALF HOUR - do NOT re-run states() on this page. The block is synchronous, so bound it from OUTSIDE the page: run the induction under a Playwright-side timeout (page.evaluate races against the harness, which is what kept killing it) or bisect the induction by calling its steps individually - dispatch the DOMContentLoaded alone first and see whether THAT is what never returns. If it is, the fix is to make the induction not re-dispatch a lifecycle event, or to guard the page init against a second run. Both are cheap once the step is identified. Row stays owed.
findings.observed: 3 x 1800s aborted; a 20s in-page setTimeout never fired, proving main-thread block rather than a pending promise; page navigates and 7 other oracles walked clean

findings.title: false-green-withdrawn 2026-08-07: banked green earlier TODAY on the claim that the APCA row covered axe's abstentions, argued from COUNTS. The exact data-wh-apca membership test refutes it: 2 of 14 abstentions are NOT in the lens's measured set (2 in page content, 0 in shared chrome), so they are judged by neither instrument. Evidence stripped; the row returns to OWED with the exact uncovered list.
findings.detail: DISPOSITIONED BY EXACT SET MEMBERSHIP, NOT BY COUNT - and that change is what makes this entry worth more than the last one. live-state-runner.js stamps every node it measures with data-wh-apca="1" precisely so a caller can ask `el.hasAttribute('data-wh-apca')` per axe abstention (:857). Its own comment states why the count argument can never work: on logbook, loading 4x the content grew the lens denominator 47->219 AND the abstentions 61->249, so the gap WIDENED - the two sets overlap without either containing the other, because the lens scopes to body-minus-shared-chrome by design while axe abstains across the chrome too. PROTOCOL RUN: the lens FIRST (so the stamps exist), then axe over the whole document, then each color-contrast INCOMPLETE node resolved via its axe target selector and asked for the stamp. 0 abstentions were unresolvable on any page, so the intersection is complete rather than sampled. WHAT THIS ROW CLAIMED AND WHY IT WAS WRONG: the banked evidence said the 14 incomplete nodes were 'counted as unjudged' and that row 142's APCA (400 measured, 0 inconclusive) covered them, concluding no text was left unjudged. That is the count argument the lens's own comment forbids, and the set test shows 2 nodes in neither instrument's denominator. THE UNCOVERED SET: 2 x td.nowrap-cell reading 'INCREASE FREQUENCY' - ordinary words, which the lens SHOULD have measured, so this one is not explained by any known exclusion and is the sharpest lead. TO CLOSE: judge those 2 nodes. They are few and characterised, so this is a small concrete task rather than a re-audit - which is the entire value of switching from a count to a set.

findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_why_refused.mjs by inducing a real 42501 and reading what the page says: 17 of 17 graded, 0 failing, and NONE blames identity for a permission problem. ★THAT LAST CLAUSE IS THE WHOLE ORACLE, and it names a defect this platform actually shipped: a 42501 'permission denied' told a SIGNED-IN buyer to sign in. findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

evidence.asserts: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state
evidence.checked: DECLARED-NA WITH A NAMED REPLACEMENT (rail R10), AND THE REASON IS THE ORACLE'S OWN WORD: MIDWAY. This oracle asks what happens when someone abandons PART-WAY THROUGH. On this page the person-caused action is generating the report, which is ONE press - there is no part-way. You either pressed it or you did not, so there is no half-applied state to leave behind and no draft to return to. ★WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PASSED: 'no half-applied state' over an action with no middle is VACUOUSLY TRUE, and a vacuous truth banked as a live-walk PASS is how coverage improves by deleting obligations. Fourteen OTHER surfaces on this platform DO have a midway - a capture modal, a composer, a multi-field form - and all fourteen were driven, filled and abandoned by reload. This page is not one of them, and the emptiness is the finding. ★THE REPLACEMENT, so the surface is not simply excused: what this page owes instead is that the effect its one press DOES cause is observable to the person who caused it - carried by effect_visible, already proven green here (PB-analytics-report-072-CF-ufai-F-V1-effect_visible). A one-press surface is still accountable; it is accountable for a different sentence. ★AND ONE PAGE WAS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED FROM THIS DISPOSITION: skillmatrix has no green effect_visible, because its exam could not be reached (SKILL_CONTENT is module-scoped and no discipline/level pair produced questions). Declaring NA there would excuse an obligation against a replacement that does not exist, which is the same vacuity wearing R10's clothes. Its rows stay owed with that diagnosis.

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs - 66 persona-journeys attempted across the roster. ★AND FIFTY OF THEM ARE NOT FINDINGS: they read 'journey could not be constructed: browser.newContext: Target page, context or browser has been closed', which is the harness dying mid-run, not a page failing a person. The run was killed twice - once by my own 570-second timeout and once when the backgrounded process lost its browser - and BOTH times it emitted those as FAILs. A probe whose browser is shot out from under it reports every remaining page as broken. ★SO THEY ARE NOT BANKED. Fifty false reds would have read as the worst finding of the session, and the only thing separating them from a real one is that I read the verdict string instead of the count. This is the same discipline as refusing a zero from a request counter a service worker was bypassing: an instrument that has stopped working reports the world as broken. ★WHAT IS BANKED IS THE SIXTEEN THAT ACTUALLY WALKED, plus the sub-journeys that completed: two_sided 15 walked / 0 failing, handoff 14 walked / 0 failing, abandon 7 walked / 1 failing. Those are real readings of a live product. FOR THIS PAGE: every journey attempt died with the harness, so nothing was measured here. Recorded as UNWALKED, never as failing - the difference between 'this page failed a person' and 'my browser closed' is the whole value of this row. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

Proven, not read: the worker's own token returns figures identical to the supervisor's.

This usually takes 5-15 seconds.' (the busy state), then 'Your session expired, so this page could not be loaded, and nothing you did was saved. Sign in again to continue.', then 'Could not generate report: JWT expired'. That third sentence names the ACTUAL cause rather than blaming the reader's connection - a distinction this codebase has had to fix before, where a rate limit was reported as a network problem. THE MOUNT RESOLVES RATHER THAN STICKING: #ar-report-mount ends holding 'Could not generate report: JWT expired', NOT the 'Compiling...' sentence, and #ar-doc is absent - so the busy state was replaced by an error and no partial report was left on screen. This also settles a concern recorded earlier in this session, where a 'Compiling analytics' message with nothing behind it looked like a stuck skeleton: under an expired session it demonstrably resolves. THE CONTROL RECOVERS: the button reads 'Generate Report' again, so a supervisor can sign in and retry. WHY THIS SETTLES ALL THREE SECTION ROWS: cover, exec+findings and predictive+action are sections of one generated document. The refusal happens before #ar-doc mounts, so NONE of the three renders - there is no partial cover with an empty findings block, which is the failure a per-section check would look for. Read-only in effect: every request was answered 401 by the harness, so no report was generated or stored.
